concepts.name: Meaning of Market
concepts.description: A market is an arrangement where buyers and sellers interact to exchange goods and services and determine prices. Markets may be physical or virtual and facilitate economic transactions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define a market and explain its role in an economy.

concepts.name: Features of a Market
concepts.description: A market consists of buyers and sellers, commodities for exchange, communication between participants, and a price mechanism that facilitates transactions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the essential features of a market.

concepts.name: Classification of Markets
concepts.description: Markets can be classified based on area, time, competition, commodities, and the nature of transactions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify markets using different economic criteria.

concepts.name: Perfect Competition
concepts.description: Perfect competition is a market structure with a large number of buyers and sellers, homogeneous products, free entry and exit, and perfect information. Individual firms have no control over market price.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the characteristics of perfect competition.

concepts.name: Monopoly
concepts.description: A monopoly exists when a single seller supplies a product with no close substitutes and faces little or no competition due to barriers to entry.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the features and implications of a monopoly market.

concepts.name: Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly
concepts.description: Monopolistic competition involves many firms selling differentiated products, whereas an oligopoly consists of a few large firms whose decisions influence one another.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare monopolistic competition and oligopoly.

concepts.name: Demand and Supply Interaction
concepts.description: Market price is determined through the interaction of demand and supply. Changes in either demand or supply influence the equilibrium price and quantity.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how demand and supply determine market price.

concepts.name: Market Equilibrium
concepts.description: Market equilibrium occurs when the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied, resulting in a stable market price.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity using demand and supply analysis.

concepts.name: Changes in Equilibrium
concepts.description: Shifts in demand or supply due to economic factors cause changes in equilibrium price and quantity in the market.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze how changes in demand or supply affect market equilibrium.

topics.title: Role of Markets in the Economy

concepts.name: Resource Allocation
concepts.description: Markets help allocate scarce resources efficiently by directing production toward goods and services demanded by consumers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how markets contribute to efficient resource allocation.

concepts.name: Competition and Consumer Welfare
concepts.description: Competition encourages efficiency, innovation, improved quality, and fair pricing, thereby benefiting consumers and promoting economic growth.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the relationship between competition and consumer welfare.

concepts.name: Government Intervention
concepts.description: Governments regulate markets to prevent unfair practices, control monopolies, protect consumers, and maintain economic stability.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the need for government intervention in different market situations.

concepts.name: Business Decision-Making
concepts.description: Businesses analyze market structures and competition to determine pricing, production, and marketing strategies.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate market structures to business decision-making.

concepts.name: Consumer Choice
concepts.description: Consumers make purchasing decisions based on price, product availability, quality, and competition within the market.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how market conditions influence consumer choices.

concepts.name: Real-World Market Examples
concepts.description: Different industries demonstrate various market structures, allowing students to connect theoretical concepts with practical economic situations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify examples of different market structures in the real economy.

concepts.name: Understanding Markets
concepts.description: This chapter introduces the meaning, classification, and structures of markets, along with price determination, market equilibrium, and the role of markets in economic development.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze market structures, explain price determination, and apply market concepts to real-world economic scenarios.
